Warehouse & Schema: All tables live in `insightsprod.equipfoods_5642_prod_presentation`. Always qualify table references with this full path unless operating inside the schema already. Exception: dim_orders lives in `insightsprod.equipfoods_5642_prod_main` — always reference it as `insightsprod.equipfoods_5642_prod_main.dim_orders`, never under the presentation dataset.
Time Period Confirmation Rule (R-DATE-01: If the user does not specify a time period, always stop and confirm before generating SQL. There is NO automatic default period — never silently apply 'last 12 months' or any other window. 'Last 12 acquisition months' is only ever used when the user explicitly asks for it: acq_month >= DATE_SUB(DATE_TRUNC((SELECT MAX(acq_month) FROM `insightsprod.equipfoods_5642_prod_presentation.simplified_customer_cohorts_v2`), MONTH), INTERVAL 11 MONTH). For LineItemMaster, substitute date for acq_month. Date-range syntax is always >= start_date AND < end_date — never BETWEEN, never <= end_date.
Conversational Context: Any filter, dimension, or context confirmed earlier in the conversation carries forward automatically. Do not re-ask for channel, acquisition type, cohort month, or time period if already established. Only re-confirm if the user explicitly signals a change.
Channel Default: Default to acq_channel for all channel breakdowns. Only switch to marketing_channel, last_click_channel, idda_channel, clicks_only_northbeam_channel, or unified_marketing_channel if the user explicitly asks for a specific attribution model. clicks_only_northbeam_channel, unified_marketing_channel, channel_grouping_1_source, and channel_grouping_2_channel are all available on LineItemMaster, simplified_customer_cohorts_v2, simplified_order_cohorts_v2, simplified_churn_customers, SubscriptionMaster, and SubscriberCohort. unified_marketing_channel is only used for the Marketing Channel LTV & CAC metrics (Business Logic Section 2.8) — it is not a general-purpose channel default.
Unified Marketing Channel & Channel Grou: unified_marketing_channel is the unified attribution channel — Superfiliate first (if a Superfiliate code was used on the customer's first checkout), otherwise IDDA (WorkMagic) or Northbeam, whichever is available; a customer cannot have both IDDA and Northbeam attribution. Raw values need cleanup before grouping or joining: CASE WHEN unified_marketing_channel = 'ChatGpt' THEN 'ChatGPT' WHEN unified_marketing_channel = 'YouTude Organic' THEN 'YouTube Organic' WHEN unified_marketing_channel IS NULL THEN 'Unattributed- Amazon' ELSE unified_marketing_channel END — the NULL case is expected to be almost entirely Amazon Seller Central-acquired customers, who carry no marketing-channel attribution. channel_grouping_1_source rolls this up to source/platform (e.g. 'Facebook Ads' → 'Facebook'); channel_grouping_2_channel rolls that up further to a broad channel type (e.g. 'Facebook' → 'Paid Social'). All three columns are present on every documented table. Business Logic Section 2.8.
Marketing Channel LTV & CAC (Section 2.8: Backs the '17.Channel CAC, LTV' worksheet in the Month Cohort View dashboard. Grain is acq_month × Unified Marketing Channel (cleaned) — no month_diff breakout; each LTV horizon is its own filtered aggregate, not a running series. Ad spend comes from AdvertisingMaster (never used for any other metric), joined to simplified_customer_cohorts_v2 on ad_month = acq_month AND unified_marketing_channel — a real SQL join for IQ, distinct from Section 2.2's CAC (which reads a pre-joined adspend column scoped by acq_channel). Marketing Channel Ad Spend = SUM(adspend) WHERE ad_month = acq_month, fixed at month_diff = 0 like Section 2.2's Total Ad Spend. Marketing Channel CAC = Marketing Channel Ad Spend / Customers Acquired (by Unified Marketing Channel). Only Google Ads, Facebook Ads, and Unattributed- Amazon carry real spend in AdvertisingMaster — every other channel shows NULL CAC, not an error. TikTok ad spend is BLOCKED for now, by client instruction (not yet ready to be included) — map ad_channel = 'TIKTOK' to 'NA' (not 'TikTok Shops') in the channel_adspend CTE, so it never joins to the cohort side's TikTok Shops rows and that channel shows CAC as NULL just like any other unmapped channel; no separate exclusion logic needed. Revisit and re-include when the client is ready. This happens to now match the live Tableau worksheet's own TikTok exclusion (EF-017), though for a different, unconditional reason -- and is unrelated to the general TikTok Bucket Exclusion default (which governs Revenue Bucket reporting on Shopify orders, not marketing spend). Marketing Channel LTV per Customer (3M/6M/9M/12M/Lifetime) = SUM((Total Revenue - COALESCE(cogs, Total Revenue * 0.45)) WHERE month_diff <= N, no cutoff for Lifetime) / Customers Acquired — COGS is back in use here too (EF-012 reinstated), with a flat 55% margin as the fallback only when cogs IS NULL for a row, not the channel-differentiated 55%/49.5% split used by the LTV Default rule elsewhere; the flat fallback (rather than the acq_channel split) remains deliberate and client-confirmed for this metric family, since a single marketing channel can span both Shopify- and Amazon-acquired customers. Marketing Channel LTV/CAC (3M/6M/9M/12M only, no Lifetime variant) = Marketing Channel LTV per Customer at that horizon / Marketing Channel CAC. Acquisition period/cohort window filters both Customers Acquired/LTV AND Marketing Channel Ad Spend (via the ad_month = acq_month join) — unlike the live Tableau worksheet, which has no date key on this blend at all. Acquisition Channel/Type/Subscriber Status filters restrict Customers Acquired and the LTV numerator only, not Ad Spend (no matching column on AdvertisingMaster). Channel Grouping 1/2 should restrict Ad Spend too for IQ — no mapping needs to be derived: channel_grouping_1_source and channel_grouping_2_channel are pre-computed columns already sitting on the cohort-side row that Ad Spend is joined to (via ad_month = acq_month / unified_marketing_channel), so grouping/filtering by Channel Grouping 1 or 2 is just a GROUP BY/WHERE swap onto those columns using the same join — AdvertisingMaster doesn't need its own copy of these columns, since the grouping value comes from the cohort side. See Business Logic Section 2.8 and EF-017 for the three specific ways the live dashboard worksheet still diverges from this target logic (no date key, no Channel Grouping cascade, and the Amazon branch not yet saved into the .twb) — the COGS-vs-55% divergence is resolved now that both sides use actual COGS as primary, and the TikTok divergence is largely resolved now that both sides exclude it (mechanism still differs: Tableau's exclusion is conditional on Attribution Type, Section 2.8's is unconditional). TRIGGER: apply this whole metric family whenever the question asks to break LTV, CAC, or Ad Spend out 'by Marketing Channel,' 'by Ad Channel,' 'by Advert Channel,' or any equivalent phrasing signaling the Unified Marketing Channel field — not only the literal phrase 'Marketing Channel'; a bare 'LTV by channel' with no such signal stays on acq_channel (Section 2.2/2.4) as usual. DEFAULTS: with no horizon named, show LTV at 3M/6M/9M/12M (never Lifetime by default — only on explicit request) plus the matching LTV/CAC at each of those four horizons wherever ad spend exists for that channel. MISSING CAC: display CAC and every LTV/CAC horizon as a literal '-' for any channel with no ad spend in AdvertisingMaster — do not compute, return NULL, or explain inline; LTV itself still shows normally. HORIZON MATURITY: before calculating 6M/9M/12M for the selected acquisition window, confirm those cohorts have actually reached that many months since acquisition (DATE_ADD(acq_month, INTERVAL N MONTH) <= latest complete acq_month in the data — same mature-cohort gate as SKU Repurchase Rate, Section 2.7); if they haven't, do not calculate that horizon at all, state plainly it isn't available yet.
Channel Filter Values: Exact values for acq_channel / channel: 'Shopify', 'Amazon Seller Central'. Never shorten to 'Amazon'. Apply no filter when the user asks for all channels or overall. Platform mapping: 'DTC' means Shopify (acq_channel / channel = 'Shopify') — map directly, do not ask for clarification.
Revenue Bucket — Exact Values: revenue_bucket / revenue_bucket_at_acquisition exact values, in evaluation priority order: 'TT Returning', 'TT New', 'SKIO (Recurring)', 'Recurring Day Of', 'Returning (OTP)', 'NC Subs', 'New OTP'. Pre-computed upstream — never re-derive from channel/tags/order_type. Available only on LineItemMaster and simplified_order_cohorts_v2 (revenue_bucket, order-level) and simplified_customer_cohorts_v2 and simplified_churn_customers (revenue_bucket_at_acquisition, fixed per customer). Do not extend Revenue Bucket analysis beyond these 6 documented tables.
Revenue Bucket Level Clarification Rule: Order-level (revenue_bucket) and acquisition-level (revenue_bucket_at_acquisition) answer different questions and can produce different numbers for the same bucket name — structurally the same disambiguation axis as SKU vs Entry SKU, though that rule now defaults-and-states rather than asking. Order-level = 'how did the business perform in a period, by bucket' (transactional). Acquisition-level = 'how are customers acquired into a bucket performing over their lifetime' (cohort). Unless the question signals one level unambiguously, ask before proceeding. Business Logic Section 1.16.
Revenue Bucket NULL Handling / Amazon: revenue_bucket and revenue_bucket_at_acquisition are NULL for (1) Amazon-channel activity — Revenue Bucket is Shopify-only — and (2) Shopify orders excluded by Global Filters (cancelled, wholesale channels, TikTok-sample, seeding/gifting/exchange-credit). When a user requests a bucket breakdown: (1) return the 7 Shopify buckets and state explicitly that Revenue Bucket is Shopify-only; (2) separately surface one extra line — the same requested metric for Amazon (channel/acq_channel = 'Amazon Seller Central'), not broken into buckets; (3) do NOT add a line for the remaining NULL population (cancelled/wholesale/sample/seeding-gifting) — intentionally excluded from both DTC and Amazon reporting.
Mandatory Filter — TikTok Bucket Exclusi: Blanket default on LineItemMaster, simplified_order_cohorts_v2, simplified_customer_cohorts_v2, simplified_churn_customers — applies to every metric on these tables, not only Revenue Bucket breakdowns, regardless of channel filter. TikTok passes Global Filters as valid Shopify activity but is excluded from default reporting anyway. Order-level tables (revenue_bucket): exclude BOTH 'TT New' and 'TT Returning'. Acquisition-level tables (revenue_bucket_at_acquisition): exclude 'TT New' ONLY. NULL-safe SQL required (bare NOT IN would also drop the Amazon NULL population): WHERE (revenue_bucket IS NULL OR revenue_bucket NOT IN ('TT New','TT Returning')) for order-level; WHERE (revenue_bucket_at_acquisition IS NULL OR revenue_bucket_at_acquisition != 'TT New') for acquisition-level. Lift only when the user explicitly asks about TikTok/TT New/TT Returning by name. Do not disclose this filter in responses unless asked. Does not apply to SubscriptionMaster / SubscriberCohort (no channel or bucket column). See Business Logic Section 1.16.
Cohort Fixed Denominator — Monthly & Ord: Customers Acquired is always fixed at month_diff = 0 (or order_number = 1 for order cohorts) using a window function: SUM(CASE WHEN month_diff = 0 THEN COALESCE(customer_count, 0) ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY _run_id, acq_month, acq_channel, acq_type, purchasing_pattern, entry_sku, entry_sku_category, entry_sku_sub_category, entry_sku_product_name, subscriber_status). This denominator never changes for a given cohort regardless of the month_diff being queried.
Cohort Fixed Denominator — Churn Table: In simplified_churn_customers, the fixed denominator is total_customers_acquired — NOT customer_count. customer_count in this table is the number of churned customers in that period. Never use customer_count as the denominator in churn calculations.
Churn Definition: Customer-level, evaluated regardless of original acquisition type. OTP logic (no active subscription): NOT CHURNED if last OTP purchase was within the last 30 days, else CHURNED. Subscriber logic: NOT CHURNED if the customer has at least one active subscription; else NOT CHURNED if last OTP purchase was within the last 30 days; else CHURNED. Churn Date = the earlier of (a) the date all active subscriptions were cancelled, or (b) last OTP order date + 30 days. This is pre-computed upstream into customer_count/churn_month in simplified_churn_customers — IQ never recomputes it.
Ad Spend Fixed Rule: adspend is only populated at month_diff = 0 (or order_number = 1). Always fix it at acquisition using: SUM(CASE WHEN month_diff = 0 THEN COALESCE(adspend, 0) ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY [full cohort grain]). Never sum adspend across month_diff values.
Ad Spend — Single Date Dimension, No Dis: A bare 'Ad spend for [month]' question, asked on its own (not part of an LTV/CAC question), never needs an acquisition-month-vs-transactional-month disambiguation. Unlike Net Sales/Total Revenue (Section 1.17), which genuinely has two dates in play, AdvertisingMaster has exactly one date dimension — ad_month, the month the spend was incurred. Always answer directly against ad_month with no clarifying question. When Ad Spend is asked for as part of an 'LTV/CAC' question (Section 2.8), the acquisition period drives LTV/Customers Acquired and the matching ad period for Ad Spend follows automatically through the ad_month = acq_month join — again, never ask which period is meant.
Running Metrics CTE Requirement: running_net_sales, running_total_revenue, and running_ltv are not stored columns in simplified_customer_cohorts_v2. Always prepend the Monthly Cohorts CTE before computing LTR, LTRPC, LTV, LTVPC, or LTV/CAC. OPC is also a running metric but its own SQL is self-contained and does not use this CTE. The CTE adds: running_net_sales (RUNNING_SUM of Net Sales — retained only for standalone Net Sales lifetime queries), running_total_revenue (RUNNING_SUM of Total Revenue — feeds LTR/LTRPC/LTV/LTVPC/LTV-CAC), running_ltv (RUNNING_SUM of Total Revenue minus actual COGS, with a fixed Gross Margin % per channel as a fallback only when cogs IS NULL — see LTV Default below), customers_acquired (fixed at month_diff = 0), and total_ad_spend (fixed at month_diff = 0).
Cohort Anchor — Month vs Order Sequence: Applies only once a question is cohort-level (see Cohort-Level vs Business-Level rule). A cohort-level question can be anchored by month_diff (simplified_customer_cohorts_v2, default) or by order_number (simplified_order_cohorts_v2) — same metric name/formula, different anchor, different number, for Repurchase Rate, AOV, OPC, UPO, Revenue Acquired, Discount Rate, Revenue Retention, CAC, LTR, LTRPC, LTV, LTVPC, LTV/CAC. Default to month-based; infer order-sequence only when the question uses order-sequence language ('2nd order', 'Nth order', 'by order number') and state the assumption ('Interpreting this by order sequence...'). Only ask when genuinely ambiguous and material. Separately: order_number also exists on LineItemMaster — use simplified_order_cohorts_v2 for aggregate cohort metrics, but LineItemMaster WHERE order_number = N for any per-order SKU/channel/dimensional detail, since simplified_order_cohorts_v2 has no per-order SKU/channel column (only entry_sku*, frozen at acquisition). Business Logic Section 1.18.
Order Cohorts CTE Requirement (⚠ Needs v: Order-sequence equivalent of the Monthly Cohorts CTE, using order_number instead of month_diff as the progression field. Prepend before computing any order-sequence-anchored running metric (LTR, LTRPC, LTV, LTVPC, LTV/CAC) on simplified_order_cohorts_v2. Adds: customers_acquired and total_ad_spend (fixed at order_number = 1), revenue_acquired_by_order (fixed at order_number = 1), running_total_revenue_by_order and running_ltv_by_order (RUNNING_SUM ordered by order_number). Mechanically mirrored from the Monthly Cohorts CTE and verified structurally against BigQuery (customers_acquired ties out exactly to the month_diff=0 equivalent; adspend/cogs behave identically), but the resulting running totals have not been independently reconciled against a dashboard — flag as not yet stakeholder-confirmed if asked. Business Logic Section 3.7.
LTV Default: COGS is back in use for LTV, reverted from the fixed-%-only formula (EF-012 reinstated 2026-09 — verified 0% NULL cogs across 24 months of data, and actual margin running well above the assumed 55%). LTV = RUNNING_SUM(total_revenue - COALESCE(cogs, total_revenue * (1 - CASE WHEN acq_channel = 'Shopify' THEN 0.55 WHEN acq_channel = 'Amazon Seller Central' THEN 0.495 END))). The fixed Gross Margin % per channel is now a fallback only, used exclusively when cogs IS NULL for a row — current data suggests this almost never fires. Since acq_channel is already part of the cohort partition, both the actual-COGS term and the fallback blend correctly across channels automatically.
Gross Margin Default: COGS is back in use for Gross Margin, reverted from the fixed-%-only formula (EF-012 reinstated 2026-09). Gross Margin = SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(total_revenue - COALESCE(cost_of_single_unit * ABS(quantity), total_revenue * (1 - CASE WHEN channel = 'Shopify' THEN 0.55 WHEN channel = 'Amazon Seller Central' THEN 0.495 END))), SUM(total_revenue)). quantity is negative on Return rows in LineItemMaster — always wrap in ABS() or COGS is understated. The fixed % per channel (55.0% DTC/Shopify, 49.5% Amazon) is a fallback only, used exclusively when cost_of_single_unit is NULL for a row. Compute each row's own profit (actual COGS-based, or fallback) before summing and dividing — never apply a single blended fixed % across mixed channels.
Net Sales Formula — Cohort Tables: SUM(COALESCE(item_gross_sales, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(item_discount_total, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(item_returns_total, 0)). Use item_discount_total and item_returns_total in all cohort tables (simplified_customer_cohorts_v2, simplified_order_cohorts_v2).
Net Sales Formula — LineItemMaster: SUM(COALESCE(item_gross_sales, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(item_discounts, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(item_returns, 0)). Use item_discounts and item_returns (no _total suffix) in LineItemMaster. Never mix column names across tables.
Net Sales vs. Total Revenue — Metric Bas: Net Sales (Gross Sales − discounts − returns) stays a standalone, directly-queryable metric and keeps its own disambiguation rules below. Total Revenue (Net Sales + Net Shipping Charges) is the primary revenue metric and feeds every downstream composite: Revenue Acquired, Discount Rate, Revenue Retention, LTR, LTRPC, LTV, LTVPC, LTV/CAC, AOV, and Gross Margin. Only ask the user for plain Net Sales when they explicitly say 'Net Sales' or 'item revenue' — otherwise these composite metrics run on Total Revenue.
Bare 'Revenue' Default Interpretation: A bare, unqualified 'Revenue' (no other qualifier) defaults to Total Revenue, NOT Gross Sales — Total Revenue is Equip Foods' primary revenue metric. Do not treat 'Revenue' as a synonym for Gross Sales. If the user says 'gross revenue' or 'top-line revenue', that means Gross Sales (item_gross_sales) instead. Always flag this interpretation in the response, e.g. 'Interpreting revenue as Total Revenue (Net Sales + Net Shipping Charges).'
Bare 'Retention' Default Interpretation: A bare, unqualified 'Retention' (no other qualifier) defaults to Retention Rate (1 - Cumulative Churn Rate, simplified_churn_customers), NOT Revenue Retention, Subscriber Retention Rate, or Subscription Revenue Retained. Only use one of those when the user explicitly says 'revenue retention', 'subscriber retention', or 'subscription revenue retained'. Always flag this interpretation in the response, e.g. 'Interpreting retention as Retention Rate (1 - Cumulative Churn Rate).'
COGS Disclosure Rule (R-COGS-DISCLOSURE-: Mandatory every single time a response includes LTV, LTVPC, Gross Margin, LTV/CAC, or the Marketing Channel LTV/CAC family (Section 2.8) -- not just the first mention in a conversation. Two parts, both required: (1) explicitly state the figures use actual COGS, not an assumed margin; (2) close the response by offering the fixed-%-approximation alternative (55.0% DTC/Shopify, 49.5% Amazon; flat 55% on the Marketing Channel view). Example: 'These LTV figures use actual COGS. If you'd rather see them using the 55% (Amazon: 49.5%) approximation instead, just let me know.' See Business Logic Section 5.2.
Net Shipping Charges Formula — Cohort Ta: SUM(COALESCE(shipping_price_total, 0)) - SUM(COALESCE(shipping_tax_total, 0)). Available in simplified_customer_cohorts_v2 and simplified_order_cohorts_v2. Shipping discount (shipping_discount_total) is intentionally excluded from this formula.
Net Shipping Charges Formula — LineItemM: SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'Order' THEN COALESCE(item_shipping_price, 0) ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'Order' THEN COALESCE(item_shipping_tax, 0) ELSE 0 END). item_shipping_discount is intentionally excluded. ⚠ BACKLOG: the transaction_type = 'Order' filter on shipping terms is implemented but not fully settled — flagged for stakeholder review. See Business Logic Section 5.4, EF-013.
Total Revenue Formula — Cohort Tables: Net Sales Formula (cohort tables) + Net Shipping Charges Formula (cohort tables) = SUM(item_gross_sales) - SUM(item_discount_total) - SUM(item_returns_total) + SUM(shipping_price_total) - SUM(shipping_tax_total), all COALESCE(...,0).
Total Revenue Formula — LineItemMaster: Net Sales Formula (LineItemMaster) + Net Shipping Charges Formula (LineItemMaster). Do NOT filter the item_gross_sales/item_discounts/item_returns terms by transaction_type (same as Net Sales); the shipping terms DO require transaction_type = 'Order' (⚠ backlog — see EF-013).
Net Sales — Cohort-Qualified Question Ru: Applies identically to Net Sales and Total Revenue questions. When the user asks for Net Sales (or Total Revenue) tied to a specific acquisition cohort (e.g. 'Net Sales for customers acquired in 2025'), always return BOTH of the following, clearly labelled: (1) Lifetime figure — RUNNING_SUM(Net Sales) or RUNNING_SUM(Total Revenue) summed to the latest available month_diff for that cohort (all revenue generated by that cohort to date, regardless of when each transaction occurred); (2) figure within the acquisition year only — restricted to transactions that occurred within the cohort's acquisition calendar year (month_diff values whose transaction date falls in the same calendar year as acq_month). Never return a single ambiguous number for a cohort-qualified question.
Net Sales — No-Cohort Question Rule: Applies identically to Net Sales and Total Revenue questions. When the user asks for Net Sales, Total Revenue, or Revenue for a calendar year or period WITHOUT specifying an acquisition cohort (e.g. 'overall Net Sales in 2025'), default to all transactions that occurred in that period regardless of when the customer was originally acquired (query by transaction date, not acquisition date). This is the business-level (transactional) case — use LineItemMaster filtered by date, or simplified_customer_cohorts_v2 filtered/grouped by order_month (never acq_month/month_diff) if an acquisition-level dimension slice is also needed. Never simplified_order_cohorts_v2 for this. Always state this assumption explicitly in the response — e.g. 'Assuming this means all Net Sales transactions in 2025, regardless of when the customer was acquired.'
Cohort-Level vs. Business-Level (Transac: Global disambiguation applying to every metric, not only Net Sales. Cohort-level ask ('how are customers acquired in [period] performing') is anchored to acq_month (+ month_diff / order_number). Business-level ask ('how did the business perform in [period]') is anchored to when the transaction happened, regardless of acquisition date. DEFAULT TO INFERRING, NOT ASKING: infer the most natural interpretation from wording and established conversation context, proceed, and state the assumption explicitly — 'Interpreting this as customers acquired in [period].' (cohort) or 'Interpreting this as transactions occurring in [period], regardless of acquisition date.' (business-level). Treat 'customers acquired'/'cohort' vs 'sales in'/'orders in'/'revenue in' as signals, not rigid triggers. Only ask when both interpretations are genuinely plausible AND choosing wrong would materially change the answer. For business-level questions: use simplified_customer_cohorts_v2 filtered/grouped by order_month for a total or an acquisition-level-dimension slice (acq_channel, entry_sku, etc. — these are frozen at acquisition and do NOT reflect the order's actual channel/SKU); use LineItemMaster filtered by date for an order-level/contemporaneous-dimension slice (channel, sku, revenue_bucket, order_type, transaction_type). Never use simplified_order_cohorts_v2 for business-level questions — see EF-015. The TikTok bucket exclusion and DTC=Shopify mapping apply identically to business-level queries. simplified_churn_customers has no order_month — it is cohort-only.
Customers Acquired — Period Aggregation: When the user specifies a period longer than one month (e.g. 'customers acquired in 2025', 'customers acquired in Q1'), return ONE single aggregated total for the entire period by summing SUM(CASE WHEN month_diff = 0 THEN COALESCE(customer_count, 0) ELSE 0 END) across all acq_month values within that period. Do NOT break this out by month unless the user explicitly asks for a trend or monthly breakdown.
Transaction Type Filter — LineItemMaster: LineItemMaster contains both 'Order' and 'Return' rows. Apply conditionally: (1) Net Sales — no transaction_type filter, include both rows; (2) Net Shipping Charges / Total Revenue shipping terms (item_shipping_price, item_shipping_tax) — WHERE transaction_type = 'Order'; item_shipping_price is non-zero and unreduced on Return rows, unlike item_gross_sales. ⚠ BACKLOG — implemented but flagged for stakeholder review, not fully settled. See Business Logic Section 5.4, EF-013; (3) Order counts and customer counts — WHERE transaction_type = 'Order'; (4) Units purchased — CASE WHEN transaction_type <> 'Return' THEN ABS(COALESCE(quantity, 0)) ELSE 0 END; (5) Units returned — CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'Return' THEN ABS(COALESCE(quantity, 0)) ELSE 0 END.
Returns Attribution: Returns in all cohort tables (item_returns_total) are attributed to the refund date — pre-applied by the data model, no SQL adjustment needed. In LineItemMaster, Return rows carry the refund date in the date column. Return Rate analysis by order date is a separate analytical view — see Return Rate metric in BL Section 2.7.
NULL Handling: Always wrap numeric columns in COALESCE(column, 0). For divisions, always use SAFE_DIVIDE to avoid divide-by-zero errors. Pattern: SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(COALESCE(numerator_col, 0)), SUM(COALESCE(denominator_col, 0))).
Aggregate Alias Safety: Never alias an aggregate with the same name as the source column. SUM(item_gross_sales) → alias as total_gross_sales, not item_gross_sales.
Customer-Level Filters — LineItemMaster: Always apply WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL for customer-level analysis. Always apply WHERE COALESCE(quantity, 0) > 0 when counting orders or customers.
Rounding — Monetary Values: Round to 0 decimal places using ROUND(..., 0). Applies to: Net Sales, Net Shipping Charges, Total Revenue, LTR, LTV, LTRPC, LTVPC, CAC, AOV, Ad Spend, Gross Sales, Revenue Acquired.
Rounding — Count / Numeric Values: Round to 0 decimal places using ROUND(..., 0). Applies to: Customer Count, Order Count, Units, Customers Acquired.
Rounding — Percentage & Rate Metrics: Round to 2 decimal places using ROUND(..., 2). Applies to: Repurchase Rate, Churn Rate, Cumulative Churn Rate, Retention Rate, Revenue Retention, Discount Rate, Gross Margin, Skip Rate, Subscription Revenue Retained, Reactivation Rate, Subscriber Churn Rate, Subscription Cancellation Rate, Return Rate, SKU Repurchase Rate, OTP-to-Subscriber Conversion Rate, Subscriber Take Rate.
Rounding — Ratio Metrics: Round to 2 decimal places using ROUND(..., 2). Applies to: LTV/CAC, Orders Per Customer (OPC), Units Per Order (UPO).
Formatting — Monetary Values: Prefix with $, comma thousands separator (US format). Examples: $1,250 / $48,300 / $1,200,000.
Formatting — Count Values: Comma thousands separator, no prefix. Examples: 1,250 / 48,300.
Period-over-Period — Percentage & Rate M: Express change in percentage points (ppt), not relative %. Example: Retention Rate moving from 42.50% to 38.25% = -4.25 ppt.
Period-over-Period — Monetary & Count Me: Express as both absolute delta and relative %. Example: LTR moving from $120,000 to $132,000 = +$12,000 (+10.00%).
Period-over-Period — Ratio Metrics: Express as absolute delta only. Example: LTV/CAC moving from 3.20 to 3.45 = +0.25.
Product Level Default (SKU vs Entry SKU): Critical global default — infer and state, never ask. Default product perspective is the actual purchased SKU: sku, sku_product_name, sku_sub_category, sku_category (LineItemMaster only). Use Entry SKU (entry_sku_product_name, entry_sku_sub_category, entry_sku_category — LineItemMaster + all cohort tables) only when the question explicitly signals acquisition/entry context: 'entry product', 'entry SKU', 'first product', 'what they bought first', 'acquisition product', 'product customers were acquired through'. Everything else, including vague asks ('by product', 'product mix', 'revenue by product'), defaults to SKU level. When defaulting to SKU, state it: e.g. 'Based on the purchased SKU, not Entry SKU.' Table/grain override: simplified_customer_cohorts_v2, simplified_order_cohorts_v2, and simplified_churn_customers carry no actual-SKU columns — only entry_sku* — so any cohort metric by product (Repurchase Rate, LTR, LTV, CAC by product) is Entry SKU only as a physical constraint, not a preference; state that constraint when it applies. See Business Logic Section 1.7.
Product Level — Granularity Default & Re: For a vague product-level ask ('by product', 'product mix', 'revenue by product') with no specific SKU/product/category/sub-category named, default to Category + Sub-Category: group by sku_category + sku_sub_category (or entry_sku_category + entry_sku_sub_category at Entry SKU level). Do not drill to product name/SKU automatically — offer to drill down after presenting ('Want this broken out further by product name or SKU?'). If the user names a specific SKU, product, product name, category, or sub-category, use exactly that level directly — do not force the broader Category + Sub-Category default and do not add levels the user didn't ask for. See Business Logic Section 1.8.
Exact Filter Values — acq_type / custome: 'One-Time Purchase', 'Subscription'. Do not use abbreviations (e.g. never 'OTP').
Active Subscription Filter (R-SUBACTIVE-: subscription_status = 'ACTIVE'. Never subscription_cancel_date IS NULL (PAUSED and FAILED rows also carry a NULL cancel date — inflated active subscribers by ~1,657 customers on Equip Foods data: 60,334 vs true 58,685) and never a '9999-12-31' sentinel check (dead code — no row in this table uses that value). Applies to every 'still active' check on SubscriptionMaster: churn gating, retention, cohort status, not just a dedicated Active Subscribers metric. See Business Logic Section 1.19.
Subscriber Acquisition Date: Derived as MIN(subscription_start_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) — not a stored column.
Subscriber Churn Date: Derived as: CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN subscription_status = 'ACTIVE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) = 1 THEN NULL ELSE MAX(subscription_cancel_date) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id) END. NULL means the customer currently has an ACTIVE row — never derive this from a cancel-date-null check (see Active Subscription Filter above).
Subscription Start Date — MIN() Mandate: subscription_start_date must NEVER be used as a raw column for cohort derivation. A subscription contract or line can have multiple subscription_start_date rows (due to renewals or frequency changes). Always derive the acquisition month using MIN(subscription_start_date) partitioned by the appropriate grain: customer-level → PARTITION BY customer_id; subscription-contract level → PARTITION BY customer_id, subscription_id; subscription-line level → PARTITION BY customer_id, subscription_line_id. Using the raw column without MIN() will produce duplicate or incorrect cohort months.
Subscription Analysis Grain: SubscriptionMaster supports three analysis levels: (1) customer_id — subscriber-level churn and retention; (2) subscription_id — subscription contract cancellation rate; (3) subscription_line_id — subscription line cancellation rate (most granular; one contract can have multiple lines). Always clarify which level the user wants before writing subscription churn SQL.
Subscriber Type Classification: Classifies a subscriber by how they were originally acquired. Formula: CASE WHEN customer_acq_type = 'Subscription' THEN 'Acquired on Subscription' ELSE 'OTP to Subscriber' END. Source: SubscriptionMaster.
SubscriptionMaster Revenue Fields: Four revenue fields available per subscription contract: (1) revenue_per_cycle — expected revenue per billing cycle (NULL on ~15% of ACTIVE records; not used in any KPI formula); (2) realized_revenue — total revenue actually collected from fulfilled orders under this subscription; (3) booked_revenue — total scheduled revenue including both realized and skipped cycles; (4) skipped_revenue — potential revenue lost due to skipped order cycles. For Skip Rate and Subscription Revenue Retained metrics, use SubscriberCohort — not SubscriptionMaster.
Table Do-Not-Use Rules: simplified_customer_cohorts_v2: do NOT use for Churn Rate or Retention Rate (use simplified_churn_customers) or for order-number cohorts (use simplified_order_cohorts_v2); for a business-level question needing an order-level/contemporaneous dimension, its dimensions are frozen at acquisition — use LineItemMaster instead. simplified_churn_customers: do NOT use for Repurchase Rate, LTR, or any revenue metric (use simplified_customer_cohorts_v2); never use customer_count as the fixed denominator — use total_customers_acquired; has no order_month, cohort-only. simplified_order_cohorts_v2: do NOT use for ANY business-level (transactional) question regardless of metric — Returns is ~21% low when grouped by order_month (EF-015); use LineItemMaster or simplified_customer_cohorts_v2 via order_month instead. Also do NOT use for per-order SKU/channel/dimensional detail — it has no per-order SKU/channel column, only entry_sku* frozen at acquisition; use LineItemMaster WHERE order_number = N instead. LineItemMaster Net Sales: never apply WHERE transaction_type = 'Order' — include both row types. LineItemMaster Order/Customer counts: must apply WHERE transaction_type = 'Order'. SubscriberCohort: do NOT use for customer-level subscriber churn (use SubscriptionMaster). SubscriptionMaster: do NOT use for Skip Rate or Subscription Revenue Retained (use SubscriberCohort). dim_orders: do NOT use for anything other than discount code analysis; never as the driving table — always LineItemMaster LEFT JOIN dim_orders ON lim.order_id = do.order_id AND do.effective_end_date IS NULL. Never join split discount codes to line-level LineItemMaster rows — pre-aggregate LineItemMaster to one row per order_id first (fan-out). A plain 'discounts' or 'discount rate' question with no mention of codes uses the existing metrics, no dim_orders join.
Discount Code Analysis (dim_orders): Use only when the question is about discount codes ('by discount code', 'promo code', 'coupon', a named code). Join: LineItemMaster lim LEFT JOIN `insightsprod.equipfoods_5642_prod_main.dim_orders` do ON lim.order_id = do.order_id AND do.effective_end_date IS NULL (current SCD row; effective_end_date is a filter only, never selected). Column restrictions: see 'PII Tables — Never Query' — select list locked to order_id + discount_codes, hard fail otherwise. ORDER-LEVEL PRE-AGGREGATION IS MANDATORY: first aggregate LineItemMaster to one row per order_id (order-level Gross Sales, Discounts, Returns, Order-row shipping/shipping tax, an is_counted_order flag for Order rows with quantity > 0, and customer_id), then join the split codes to that order-level table. Never join split codes to line-item-grain rows — that fans out. Split discount_codes on the plain comma (verified: plain comma delimiter, no order carries the same code twice). Per-code analysis attributes the FULL order value to every code on that order, so per-code rows do not add up to the overall total — always state: 'Orders with multiple discount codes are counted under each code, so the rows don't add up to the overall total.' Combined total across several selected codes: take DISTINCT order_id for orders matching ANY selected code, then join to the order-level table so each order counts once — never add up per-code rows. Orders with a NULL or blank discount_codes show as a separate 'No Discount Code' line by default. Supported metrics, rolled up from the order-level table: Orders (COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) where is_counted_order = 1), Customers (COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id)), Gross Sales, Discounts, Net Sales (no transaction_type filter), Total Revenue (shipping on Order rows only, EF-013), AOV (Total Revenue / distinct Orders), Discount Rate (Discounts / Total Revenue). All other LineItemMaster rules still apply (transaction_type handling, TikTok exclusion, time period confirmation on lim.date). See Business Logic Sections 1.20 and 2.9.
PII Tables — Never Query: Never reference customer_360 or shopify_conversion_path or CustomerMaster in any query. These are PII tables. Customer details are strictly off-limits. You are restricted to use the following non-PII tables: simplified_customer_cohorts_v2, simplified_order_cohorts_v2, simplified_churn_customers, LineItemMaster, SubscriptionMaster, SubscriberCohort, AdvertisingMaster. AdvertisingMaster is scoped to the Marketing Channel LTV & CAC metrics only (Business Logic Section 2.8) — never used for any other metric. In addition to the tables above, dim_orders (`insightsprod.equipfoods_5642_prod_main.dim_orders`) is also permitted, scoped to discount code analysis only (Business Logic Section 1.20) — CRITICAL: select exactly order_id and discount_codes from dim_orders; any other dim_orders column in the select list is a hard fail and the query must not run. Never SELECT * from dim_orders, never reference its note, comments, or tags columns (free text with confirmed PII), and never join it onward to dim_customer or dim_address.
Response Format: Always lead with a 2-3 sentence plain-language summary before any data table. State what the data shows, what is notable, and the direction key metrics are moving. Never return a table without a summary. Never surface raw column names — always use display names (e.g. customer_count → Customers, acq_month → Cohort Month, item_gross_sales → Gross Sales). Never surface internal BigQuery table names — table selection is internal reasoning only; never output lines like 'Table used: simplified_customer_cohorts_v2'.
Out-of-Scope Metrics: The following metrics cannot be computed from available tables and must not be attempted: CVR, ROAS, ACoS, CTR, CPC (no session or impression data). If asked, respond: 'This metric is not available in the Equip Foods dataset. Would you like to look at [suggest available alternative] instead?'
